### 2. Scope of Commissioning

1. Inverter electrical installation and termination integrity

### 4. Electrical Installation Verification

#### 4.1 DC Side

#### 5.2 Battery Bank Configuration

Battery Bank B-12 was connected to the inverter's DC bus. The manufacturer spec for Battery Bank
B-12 indicates capacity_kwh of 1200 kWh. Record status: current. This value was entered as the
nominal energy capacity in the inverter's energy management settings and cross-referenced against
the battery data sheet (Battery Bank B-12 Data Sheet, Doc. No. BB12-DS-001, Rev. 2, dated January
2019).
The inverter enclosure was inspected for physical damage, corrosion, and proper sealing. The IP54-rated enclosure was found to be in good condition with all gaskets intact. Door hinges and latches operated smoothly. The desiccant cartridge was replaced during commissioning (new cartridge installed, Part No. SM-DSC-200) as the original showed slight discoloration indicating moisture ingress during transit.

### 2.2 Mounting and Clearances

The inverter was mounted on the concrete plinth at a height of 300 mm above finished floor level. All four mounting brackets were secured with M12 stainless steel anchors torqued to 45 N·m. Clearances around the enclosure were verified as follows:

### 2.3 Cooling System

Ambient temperature at the time of inspection was 31°C, which is within the inverter's specified operating range of -10°C to +50°C.

## 3. Electrical Testing

### 3.1 Insulation Resistance Testing

### 3.3 DC Side Checks

## 4. System Configuration

### 4.2 Battery Bank Configuration

**Reviewed by:** A. Bello (Senior Engineer, SolarMax West Africa)
**Customer Representative:** Alhaji I. Suleiman (Kano State Rural Electrification Agency)

---

### 5. Functional Testing

#### 5.1 Pre-Energisation Checks

Prior to energisation, a final visual inspection was carried out. All cable glands were verified tight, all covers and doors secured, and all warning labels in place. Torque checks on the DC and AC terminals were repeated per the installation manual torque table (Appendix B of this report). No loose connections were found.

The inverter's internal cooling fans were checked for free rotation. Two fans (rear top, positions F1 and F2) were found to have a slight resistance to manual rotation. These were not replaced at this stage as the resistance was minor and the fans were within the manufacturer's specification for start-up. A note was added to the site maintenance log to re-check fan operation at the next scheduled inspection.

#### 5.2 Energisation Sequence

The energisation was performed in the following sequence:

1.  AC grid supply breaker (MCCB-1) closed. Inverter display powered up.
2.  Inverter start-up self-test initiated automatically. All internal checks passed.
3.  DC string isolators (DC-1 through DC-8) closed one at a time.
4.  After all 8 strings were connected, the inverter entered "Waiting for Grid" mode.
5.  Grid voltage and frequency were confirmed within the acceptable window by the inverter's internal monitoring.

The inverter's initial DC input voltage was 612 V. This is within the MPPT operating window of 400–820 V.

#### 5.3 Grid Connection and Load Test

The inverter synchronised with the grid and began exporting power at 09:47 local time. The system was run in grid-tied mode for 2 hours without fault.

A load bank test was then conducted to verify output at various power levels. The results are recorded in the table below.

| Time | Output Power (kW) | Output Current (A) | Voltage (V) | Frequency (Hz) | Inverter Temp (°C) | Remarks |
|------|-------------------|--------------------|-------------|----------------|--------------------|---------|
| 09:47 | 0.5 | 2.1 | 398 | 50.0 | 31 | Start-up export |
| 10:15 | 25.0 | 36.8 | 397 | 50.0 | 38 | Steady state |
| 10:45 | 50.0 | 73.5 | 396 | 50.0 | 44 | Load bank 1 |
| 11:15 | 75.0 | 110.2 | 395 | 50.0 | 49 | Load bank 2 |
| 11:45 | 100.0 | 147.0 | 394 | 50.0 | 54 | Load bank 3, full load |

All output parameters remained within the manufacturer's specified limits. The inverter temperature at full load (54°C) was below the maximum allowable of 60°C. The cooling fans operated continuously during the test.

#### 5.4 Anti-Islanding Test

The anti-islanding protection was tested by opening the grid supply breaker (MCCB-1) while the inverter was exporting 100 kW. The inverter detected the grid loss and shut down in 0.4 seconds. This is within the required 2-second disconnection time. The inverter displayed "Grid Loss" and did not attempt to reconnect for the duration of the 5-minute reconnection timer.

#### 5.5 Battery Backup Test

The battery backup function was tested by simulating a grid outage. The grid supply breaker was opened, and the inverter was observed to transfer to battery backup mode. The changeover was seamless, with no interruption to the connected critical loads (site lighting and control systems).
SolarMax Inverter SX-500 Commissioning Report

**Site:** Ijebu-Ode Solar Farm, Ogun State  
**Inverter Serial No:** SX5-2019-8842  
**Inverter Firmware at Commissioning:** v2.4.1  
**Report Date:** 12 March 2020  
**Prepared by:** T. Adeyemi, Commissioning Engineer  
**Approved by:** M. Okafor, Site Manager

---

### 6. Battery Backup Test (Continued)

The changeover to battery backup occurred within 20 ms and was verified by a power quality analyser connected to the critical load panel. The inverter remained in battery backup mode for 35 minutes, during which the battery state of charge dropped from 98% to 91%. The connected loads (site lighting, control systems, and two security cameras) operated without interruption.

At the end of the test, the grid supply breaker was re-closed. The inverter detected the return of grid supply and re-synchronised before transferring back to grid-tied mode. The re-transfer was completed without any glitch on the critical loads.

**Battery backup test results:**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Load during backup | 12.4 kW |
| Transfer time | 20 ms |
| Battery voltage at start | 512 V |
| Battery voltage at end | 508 V |
| Backup duration | 35 min |
| Battery SOC at start / end | 98% / 91% |
| Re-sync time after grid return | 2.1 s |

---

### 7. Communication and Monitoring Setup

The inverter was connected to the site SCADA system via the built-in Ethernet port. The following communication settings were configured:

| Parameter | Setting |
|-----------|---------|
| IP address | 192.168.10.54 |
| Subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
| Gateway | 192.168.10.1 |
| Modbus TCP port | 502 |
| Protocol | Modbus TCP / SunSpec |

The inverter was registered with the monitoring portal under site ID **IJB-OG-001**. Communication was verified by polling the inverter's live data every 5 seconds for 30 minutes. No communication dropouts were observed.

The following data points were confirmed as reporting correctly to the portal:

- AC output power (kW)
- DC input voltage (V)
- DC input current (A)
- Inverter temperature (°C)
- Total energy export (kWh)
- Grid frequency (Hz)
- Status flags (running, fault, grid loss, battery mode)

A screenshot of the portal dashboard was taken and saved in the project folder as `IJB_OG_001_dashboard_12032020.png`.

---

### 8. Firmware Update Procedure and Version History

The inverter was delivered with firmware v2.3.0 installed. Before commissioning, the firmware was updated to v2.4.1 following the procedure in the SolarMax service manual (document SM-SX5-FW-02 Rev C).

**Firmware update procedure used:**

1. Downloaded firmware package `SX500_v2.4.1.zip` from the SolarMax support portal (checksum verified against published MD5).
2. Transferred the package to a laptop and extracted the `.sxf` update file.
3. Connected the laptop to the inverter's service USB port.
4. Initiated the update from the inverter's local display menu (Settings → System → Firmware Update).
5. The update process took approximately 12 minutes. The inverter displayed "Updating – Do Not Power Off" during the process.
6. After the update, the inverter rebooted automatically and displayed the new firmware version on the startup screen.

**Firmware version history for SX-500 series:**

| Version | Release Date | Key Changes |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| v2.1.0 | Jun 2019 | Initial production release |
| v2.2.0 | Sep 2019 | Added Modbus register for reactive power setpoint |
| v2.3.0 | Dec 2019 | Improved anti-islanding detection algorithm |
| v2.4.0 | Feb 2020 | Fixed communication dropout issue on some units |
| v2.4.1 | Mar 2020 | Minor bug fix for battery SOC reporting; corrected temperature offset in some units |

documents.content:
## SolarMax Inverter SX-500 Commissioning Report

**Project:** Kano State Rural Electrification – Phase 2 (Site K-7)
**Inverter Serial No:** SX5-19-04471
**Report No:** COM-SX5-019-047
**Date:** 14 November 2019
**Prepared by:** M. Okafor (Lead Commissioning Engineer)
**Reviewed by:** A. Bello (Senior Engineer, SolarMax West Africa)
**Customer Representative:** Alhaji I. Suleiman (Kano State Rural Electrification Agency)

---

### 5. Functional Testing

#### 5.1 Pre-Energisation Checks

Prior to energisation, a final visual inspection was carried out. All cable glands were verified tight, all covers and doors secured, and all warning labels in place. Torque checks on the DC and AC terminals were repeated per the installation manual torque table (Appendix B of this report). No loose connections were found.

The inverter's internal cooling fans were checked for free rotation. Two fans (rear top, positions F1 and F2) were found to have a slight resistance to manual rotation. These were not replaced at this stage as the resistance was minor and the fans were within the manufacturer's specification for start-up. A note was added to the site maintenance log to re-check fan operation at the next scheduled inspection.

#### 5.2 Energisation Sequence

The energisation was performed in the following sequence:

1.  AC grid supply breaker (MCCB-1) closed. Inverter display powered up.
2.  Inverter start-up self-test initiated automatically. All internal checks passed.
3.  DC string isolators (DC-1 through DC-8) closed one at a time.
4.  After all 8 strings were connected, the inverter entered "Waiting for Grid" mode.
5.  Grid voltage and frequency were confirmed within the acceptable window by the inverter's internal monitoring.

The inverter's initial DC input voltage was 612 V. This is within the MPPT operating window of 400–820 V.

#### 5.3 Grid Connection and Load Test

The inverter synchronised with the grid and began exporting power at 09:47 local time. The system was run in grid-tied mode for 2 hours without fault.

A load bank test was then conducted to verify output at various power levels. The results are recorded in the table below.

| Time | Output Power (kW) | Output Current (A) | Voltage (V) | Frequency (Hz) | Inverter Temp (°C) | Remarks |
|------|-------------------|--------------------|-------------|----------------|--------------------|---------|
| 09:47 | 0.5 | 2.1 | 398 | 50.0 | 31 | Start-up export |
| 10:15 | 25.0 | 36.8 | 397 | 50.0 | 38 | Steady state |
| 10:45 | 50.0 | 73.5 | 396 | 50.0 | 44 | Load bank 1 |
| 11:15 | 75.0 | 110.2 | 395 | 50.0 | 49 | Load bank 2 |
| 11:45 | 100.0 | 147.0 | 394 | 50.0 | 54 | Load bank 3, full load |

All output parameters remained within the manufacturer's specified limits. The inverter temperature at full load (54°C) was below the maximum allowable of 60°C. The cooling fans operated continuously during the test.

#### 5.4 Anti-Islanding Test

The anti-islanding protection was tested by opening the grid supply breaker (MCCB-1) while the inverter was exporting 100 kW. The inverter detected the grid loss and shut down in 0.4 seconds. This is within the required 2-second disconnection time. The inverter displayed "Grid Loss" and did not attempt to reconnect for the duration of the 5-minute reconnection timer.

#### 5.5 Battery Backup Test

The battery backup function was tested by simulating a grid outage. The grid supply breaker was opened, and the inverter was observed to transfer to battery backup mode. The changeover was seamless, with no interruption to the connected critical loads (site lighting and control systems).

documents.content:
SolarMax Inverter SX-500 Commissioning Report

**Site:** Ijebu-Ode Solar Farm, Ogun State  
**Inverter Serial No:** SX5-2019-8842  
**Inverter Firmware at Commissioning:** v2.4.1  
**Report Date:** 12 March 2020  
**Prepared by:** T. Adeyemi, Commissioning Engineer  
**Approved by:** M. Okafor, Site Manager

---

### 6. Battery Backup Test (Continued)

The changeover to battery backup occurred within 20 ms and was verified by a power quality analyser connected to the critical load panel. The inverter remained in battery backup mode for 35 minutes, during which the battery state of charge dropped from 98% to 91%. The connected loads (site lighting, control systems, and two security cameras) operated without interruption.

At the end of the test, the grid supply breaker was re-closed. The inverter detected the return of grid supply and re-synchronised before transferring back to grid-tied mode. The re-transfer was completed without any glitch on the critical loads.

**Battery backup test results:**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Load during backup | 12.4 kW |
| Transfer time | 20 ms |
| Battery voltage at start | 512 V |
| Battery voltage at end | 508 V |
| Backup duration | 35 min |
| Battery SOC at start / end | 98% / 91% |
| Re-sync time after grid return | 2.1 s |

---

### 7. Communication and Monitoring Setup

The inverter was connected to the site SCADA system via the built-in Ethernet port. The following communication settings were configured:

| Parameter | Setting |
|-----------|---------|
| IP address | 192.168.10.54 |
| Subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
| Gateway | 192.168.10.1 |
| Modbus TCP port | 502 |
| Protocol | Modbus TCP / SunSpec |

The inverter was registered with the monitoring portal under site ID **IJB-OG-001**. Communication was verified by polling the inverter's live data every 5 seconds for 30 minutes. No communication dropouts were observed.

The following data points were confirmed as reporting correctly to the portal:

- AC output power (kW)
- DC input voltage (V)
- DC input current (A)
- Inverter temperature (°C)
- Total energy export (kWh)
- Grid frequency (Hz)
- Status flags (running, fault, grid loss, battery mode)

A screenshot of the portal dashboard was taken and saved in the project folder as `IJB_OG_001_dashboard_12032020.png`.

---

### 8. Firmware Update Procedure and Version History

The inverter was delivered with firmware v2.3.0 installed. Before commissioning, the firmware was updated to v2.4.1 following the procedure in the SolarMax service manual (document SM-SX5-FW-02 Rev C).

**Firmware update procedure used:**

1. Downloaded firmware package `SX500_v2.4.1.zip` from the SolarMax support portal (checksum verified against published MD5).
2. Transferred the package to a laptop and extracted the `.sxf` update file.
3. Connected the laptop to the inverter's service USB port.
4. Initiated the update from the inverter's local display menu (Settings → System → Firmware Update).
5. The update process took approximately 12 minutes. The inverter displayed "Updating – Do Not Power Off" during the process.
6. After the update, the inverter rebooted automatically and displayed the new firmware version on the startup screen.

**Firmware version history for SX-500 series:**

| Version | Release Date | Key Changes |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| v2.1.0 | Jun 2019 | Initial production release |
| v2.2.0 | Sep 2019 | Added Modbus register for reactive power setpoint |
| v2.3.0 | Dec 2019 | Improved anti-islanding detection algorithm |
| v2.4.0 | Feb 2020 | Fixed communication dropout issue on some units |
| v2.4.1 | Mar 2020 | Minor bug fix for battery SOC reporting; corrected temperature offset in some units |
